sources.citation: Blench, Roger. Alumic languages index page (rogerblench.info/Language/Niger-Congo/BC/Plateau/Alumic/AluOP.htm), Wayback capture 2025-05-23 — lists as the only Akpondu item.
sources.note: Index page only; confirms no further Akpondu material was ever posted.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, David Onoja, Innocent Jonah, John Muniru & Samuel Eju. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Arum (Alumu-Tesu) [aab] and Atoro [tdv] Languages of Nasarawa State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-048. SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing on Akpondu beyond noting (after Blench 2019:vi) that it was related to Arum and is now extinct.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019 [2020 printout]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition IV. Entry 15 'Akpondu [†]'.
sources.note: Nothing; entry says '1 (2005). The last speaker was only a remember[er] and can only recall fragmentary vocabulary'; classification Plateau: Alumic; source Blench & Kato (2005).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Barau Kato. 2012 [fieldwork Aug 2005]. Akpondu, Nigbo, Bəbər and Nisam: moribund or extinct languages of Central Nigeria. Ms., Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Jos, 11 June 2012. 4 pp. (the only primary record of Akpondu; = Glottolog's 'Blench 2005', ref 96017, and the Atlas of Nigerian Languages' 'Blench & Kato 2005')
sources.note: Nothing. The document is a survey note plus numerals 1-11 recalled by the village head of Babur (Akpondu), the last rememberer, who 'can only remember how to count but not to speak in sentences'; forms are tone-marked but there is no phonological commentary of any kind.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Barau Kato. 2012. The Təsu language of Central Nigeria and its affinities (draft, KWEF) — closest documented relative (Alumu-Təsu, alum1246); sec. 3.3 'three level tones', no stress statement.
